partnershipPlan: Two patient partners and one carer partner review the interview guides before the REB application and the themes before reporting.
socialListening: No social media listening; the program's compliments and complaints log from the last year is read for mentions of night-time calls.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: At two in the morning his breathing changed and I did not know whether that was the team's job or the ambulance's.
items.implication: Explore the night-time plan and the night line in every carer interview.

items.theme: Not wanting to be a bother
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They told me to ring any time, but it felt wrong to wake a nurse for something that might be nothing.
items.implication: Ask about reluctance to call as well as delays in answering.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: When I am on call and have never met the patient, sending them in is the safe choice.
items.implication: Interview night clinicians about handover content.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: By the fourth night I had not slept, and I think that is why we ended up back in hospital.
items.implication: Treat carer strain as a pathway to readmission, not as a patient characteristic.

summary: Four composite voices on night calls, reluctance, unfamiliar patients and carer exhaustion.
